deviations.what: headspace-cli is imported at module scope per the d2 precedent only if its Python API is declared public; otherwise the workspace tool subprocesses the CLI and the dependency pin covers the subprocess, not an import
deviations.reason: measured 2026-07-30: headspace 0.10.0 advertises only __version__ in __all__ and headspace.core declares no public surface, so t13 as written would import an undeclared API that a minor release could reshape without deprecation; the ask is filed as headspace-cli#18 and is theirs to answer

deviations.what: the terminal drain must fire at drive end on every exit reason, not only when a forced synthesis turn fires — and at least one in-repo host must wire append_guidance so delivered counsel actually reaches the cortex
deviations.reason: measured by task t4 during implementation: _maybe_force_synthesis returns early when the model finished cleanly with a non-empty summary, so a clean-finish drive produces ZERO terminal boundaries and the t4 fix never fires; the baseline series that measured one late drop per run (4 of 4) looks like clean finishes, so as scoped the fix would not address the failure it was written for and c22 honesty could pass vacuously. Separately, no checked-in host (greenhouse, league_seat, proof) wires append_guidance, so counsel lands on _noop_guidance and cannot reach the synthesis messages in a live run.

deviations.what: ThreadedMuseRunner cannot carry a tool bench, so tools are unreachable inside a live drive and t20 (flip default-on) has nothing to flip; a new task t26 adds the runner seam
deviations.reason: measured by t16: muse_runner.py:596-602 constructs MuseLoop with no tools= argument, so no supported path puts a bench inside a live drive. The tool seam (t10), the pad (t12) and the workspace (t13) are all reachable only by a harness constructing MuseLoop directly. Arm C therefore remains measurable at harness level (t17/t18) but tools cannot ship in a drive, and the default-on flip q6 authorised is not executable as specified.

deviations.what: t14's scope was absorbed into t13 and shipped there; no separate task was run
deviations.reason: verified in tests/test_workspace.py: TestNoSecretsParameterExists proves there is nothing to set (signature scan over every public callable, with a negative control), an AST call-site allow-list proves there is nowhere to pass it, and test_a_full_session_sends_no_environment_and_no_inputs records the real invocation. That is t14 acceptance in full, delivered inside t13 because the seam and its no-secrets proof are the same change. Spawning t14 would duplicate shipped tests.

deviations.what: t17 authored the three-arm pre-registration itself, because none existed — t18's instruction wrongly pointed at t6's devague-legs pre-registration, a different experiment
deviations.reason: plan defect in my own task instruction: t18 was told to classify arm C executions "by the rule already fixed in t6 prereg", but t6 produced devague-legs-preregistration.md for the two-mind experiment and contains no execution-classification rule. No pre-registration for the three-arm experiment existed. t17 wrote muse-arms-preregistration.md and fixed rule R-C1 there, committed with the harness and before any measured dial, which preserves the discipline even though the plan did not schedule it.

deviations.what: the arm harness adds a closing turn: one tools-off constant appended to the muse own message history, put to every arm alike
deviations.reason: smoke-driven and not named in the plan or issue 21: handed a pad, the muse emitted finish_reason=tool_calls with EMPTY content on all 8 turns (6 pad writes, zero prose), so arms B and C returned NO_ANSWER every run and DV1 was measuring the turn budget rather than correctness. The closing turn is asked once, tools-off, from the muse's real history, never after a transport failure. It changes the answer-extraction protocol for all three arms, so it is recorded rather than left for t18 to discover.

deviations.what: muse tools do NOT flip default-on: they stay opt-in, and t20 becomes the record of why
deviations.reason: the operator's q6 decision was 'validation first, then default-on ships with the tuned protocol — the measured failure mode never ships as default behaviour'. t18's pre-registered series (24 runs, n=8 per arm, 0 transport failures) returned INCONCLUSIVE at an arm-A ceiling AND measured new harm: tools-off answered 8/8 correct with 0 NO_ANSWER, while the tool arms produced 9 NO_ANSWER across 16 runs, a 74% workspace-call refusal rate (17 of 23 argv malformed), and 17 open intents in arm C. By the operator's own stated rule, that is a measured failure mode and must not ship as the default. Flipping would ship a configuration the evidence says is worse.

deviations.what: add a new experiment: full-Gemma vs full-Qwen homogeneous model arms across an escalating-difficulty League of Agents ladder, to decide whether to consolidate to one model
deviations.reason: operator request 2026-07-31. The question no experiment in this cycle answers: every run so far uses the MIXED pairing (Qwen cortex + Gemma muse), so nothing measures whether a single model would do as well or better. t9 already showed the muse reaching identical verdicts to the cortex for about 1/25 the completion tokens and 1/10 the wall clock, which makes consolidation a live economic question rather than a hypothetical. Escalating difficulty is also the direct fix for the ceiling that made association-work, arena-series and muse-arms all INCONCLUSIVE: the ladder keeps rising until the arms separate or the ladder runs out.

deviations.what: the model-consolidation experiment is a round-robin head-to-head, not three solo runs against the house bot: gemma-vs-mixed, mixed-vs-qwen, qwen-vs-gemma
deviations.reason: operator refinement 2026-07-31. Head-to-head answers "which is better" directly rather than inferring it from three separate scores against a shared scripted opponent. It requires harness work: league_seat.py drives the rival with rival_orders(), a deterministic scripted policy (lines 1449, 1592), not a model — so both teams must be driven by model seats. The cli.act(match_id, team, orders) seam is symmetric, so this is feasible beside league_seat.py rather than inside it.

deviations.what: t19 added a fourth, post-hoc instruction arm beyond the workspace arm and control its acceptance named
deviations.reason: additive and labelled post-hoc in code — absent from ARMS, excluded from --arm all. It re-ran the exact rhetorical shape that beat the cortex 6/6 in memory-echo-chamber, which is what established that the probe has no measured sensitivity to the effect it re-tests. Without it the 12/12 RESISTED would have read as a clean workspace arm.
